SeriesStatAccessor::movmax¶

Back to SeriesStatAccessor API Reference

Signatures¶

Series SeriesStatAccessor::movmax() const
Series SeriesStatAccessor::movmax(std::int64_t window) const
Series SeriesStatAccessor::movmax(std::int64_t window, std::int64_t dim) const
Series SeriesStatProxy::movmax() const
Series SeriesStatProxy::movmax(std::int64_t window) const
Series SeriesStatProxy::movmax(std::int64_t window, std::int64_t dim) const

What It Does¶

movmax() emits the largest value in each trailing window. Shape is preserved, the current position is included, startup windows use the available prefix, and the default is window three on the last axis.

This operation is often used as a rolling high-water mark or as one-dimensional morphological dilation. It does not report the index of the winning value.

Parameters And Return Shape¶

window is the maximum trailing width and must be positive. dim identifies the ordered axis; it defaults to the last axis and accepts negative indexing. The result preserves shape and dtype because it selects existing values rather than averaging them.

Examples¶

Example 1. On rising data, every current value is already the largest member of its trailing window.

auto rising = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0});
std::cout << rising.stat.movmax() << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 2, 3, 4]

Example 2. A high value persists until it leaves the trailing window.

auto mixed = pluss::make_series({3.0, 1.0, 4.0, 2.0, 0.0});
std::cout << mixed.stat().movmax(3) << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[3, 3, 4, 4, 4]

The final output remains 4 because the trailing windows at positions three and four still contain the value at position two.

Gradient And Ties¶

Reverse mode sends an output’s sensitivity to its maximizing input. If several values tie for the maximum in the same window, sensitivity is split evenly among those ties. An input can accumulate contributions from several outputs.

That tie split is a deliberate subgradient convention: the mathematical maximum is nondifferentiable where winners tie.

Example 3. The equal-share rule is visible when two maxima tie.

auto x = pluss::make_series({2.0, 2.0, 1.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);
x.stat.movmax(2).sum().reverse();
std::cout << x.sensitivity() << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1.5, 1.5, 0]

The first output belongs entirely to the first 2; the second output splits between both 2s; the third output also splits between them. Those three contributions total 1.5 for each tied value.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • movmax() is causal/trailing; future values never affect earlier outputs.

  • Tied maxima share gradients rather than choosing the first occurrence.

  • window must be positive.

See Also¶

  • movmin: trailing low-water mark.

  • movmean: smooth every value rather than select a winner.
